text:
maya: quick sketch of a measurement protocol for bringing up speculative decoding on a new quantized build — want quick feedback before i formalize into a runbook

jon: +1, paste it here. main concerns: bias/regression surface and reproducibility.

maya: short version: do paired A/B runs on identical hardware and workload, keep seeds + request ordering the same, collect token-level and end-to-end quality metrics, and a small human review sample for hallucination cases. we should treat quant variant + speculative params as a single treatment vector.

ravi: what do you mean by "paired" exactly? single process alternating requests?

maya: paired = fork two identical runners (control: speculative=false, treatment: speculative=true) and replay the exact same request list in the same order to each. we record per-request outputs, p50/p95 latencies (cold vs warm), GPU utilization, and token counts. important: re-seed RNGs and record seed. if ordering nondeterminism possible, run a deterministic replay harness that pins ordering.

sophie: metrics list?

maya: proposed metrics (short):
- latency: p50/p90/p95 end-to-end, per-token latency, cold (first token) vs warm (steady-state)
- throughput: tokens/sec (batched and single-request)
- quality: token-level cross-entropy delta, token F1 (against references for QA/summarization), EM for span QA, BLEU/ROUGE for pairwise tasks, and embedding-based cosine agreement to detect semantic drift
- safety/hallucination: hallucination rate heuristics + sample human review (n=200 stratified)
- stability: inter-run variability across 5 seeds (report stddev and 95% CI via bootstrap)
- failure modes: fallback frequency (how often speculative path aborted to baseline), and latency spikes correlated to fallback

derek: add a simple delta-acceptance rule: if any core metric (EM or token-F1 for that workload) drops by >0.5% absolute and is statistically significant (p < 0.05 bootstrap) reject rollout. also flag if hallucination-rate increases >1ppt.

maya: yes — and for multiple tasks apply Benjamini-Hochberg across families to avoid false positives. specify primary metric per workload ahead of time.

jon: implementation details? how do we run the experiments reproducibly across quant variants (fp16 vs int8 + qkv-tail)?

maya: run matrix: for each model build (fp16 baseline, int8-static, int8-dynamic, qkv-tail), do control/treatment pair. keep hardware identical (same GPU type, same driver/cuda), same batch sizes. warmup: run 200 short prompts to populate KV cache before measurement window. measurement window = next 2000 requests. store raw responses and perf traces to s3://redwood-infer-experiments/spec-decode/{build}/{spec-params}/{run_ts}/

ravi: sample command for the developer bench?

maya: posted a minimal curl example:
```
curl -s -X POST https://local-runner:8080/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"our-13b-int8","speculative":true,"speculator_beams":2,"seed":42,"input":"Summarize: ..."}' \
```
we also write an orchestration YAML for the replay harness that pins ordering and seeds.

sophie: how do we do significance testing across paired outputs?

maya: primary approach = paired bootstrap: resample request indices with replacement, compute metric delta per resample, get 95% CI. also compute per-request agreement (exact match / token edit distance) and report distribution. for corpus-level metrics like ROUGE use paired bootstrap too.

derek: for latency comparisons use nonparametric test (wilcoxon signed-rank) on per-request p50s; but we mostly care about tail regressions, so include p95 tail-plot and waterfall traces for anomalies.

maya: ops note: keep a canary cutoff: if fallback rate > 2% or p95 latency doubles vs baseline, abort runs and collect full trace for first 500 anomalies. automate alert to #eng-oncall with a small JSON summary.

eval-bot: automated run summary uploaded: s3://redwood-infer-experiments/spec-decode/8765432199/summary.json — control: fp16, treatment: int8+spec(beam=2)
eval-bot: quick numbers: delta EM = -0.12% (CI [-0.45, +0.21]) not significant; p95 latency delta = -18% (improvement); fallback rate = 0.6%

ravi: nice. can we also log token-confidence drift? i want to see if spec path changes calibration.

maya: added token confidence histograms and calibration slope/entropy diffs to the outputs. we surface those in the model-dashboard under per-build diffs.

sophie: next steps: maya please turn this into a runbook with the orchestration YAML + a checklist for SRE to stand up benchmark runners. i can help write the BH correction code and dashboard panels.

maya: will do. thanks all — i’ll post the runbook PR and tag you for review. :pray:
